<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000527_dcnt_02912537-28e5-4016-b9f6-cafc83e44e4a" continuedAt="F_000527_dcnt_15c605dc-a634-47a0-a0ae-d82df516ede8"><ix:continuation id="F_000575_cnt_1">
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Under the new revenue standard, we <span style="color:#000000;">recognize revenue upon the delivery of ITCs to investors under our lease pass-through fund arrangements as this is the point in time that control of ITCs has transferred</span>.</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We indemnify the investors for any recapture of ITCs due to our non-compliance. We have concluded that the likelihood of a recapture event is remote, and consequently, we have not recognized a liability for this indemnification on the consolidated balance sheets.</p></ix:continuation><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000577" name="tsla:TaxIncentivePolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001318605_20190101_20191231" escape="true">
<p style="margin-top:13pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Nevada Tax Incentives</p>
<p style="margin-top:4pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We had entered into agreements with the State of Nevada and Storey County in Nevada that provide abatements for sales, use, real property, personal property and employer excise taxes, discounts to the base tariff energy rates and transferable tax credits. These incentives are available for the applicable periods beginning on <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000824" name="tsla:IncentiveBeginningPeriod" contextRef="C_0001318605_us-gaapGuaranteeObligationsByNatureAxis_tslaGigafactoryMember_20190101_20191231" format="ixt:datemonthdayyearen">October&#160;17, 2014</ix:nonNumeric> and ending on either <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000825" name="tsla:IncentiveEndingPeriod" contextRef="C_0001318605_us-gaapGuaranteeObligationsByNatureAxis_tslaGigafactoryMember_20190101_20191231" format="ixt:datemonthdayyearen">June 30, 2024</ix:nonNumeric> or June&#160;30, 2034 (depending on the incentive). Under these agreements, we were eligible for a maximum of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000826" name="tsla:MaximumEligibleAmountOfTransferableInvestmentTaxCredits" contextRef="C_0001318605_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_us-gaapGuaranteeObligationsByNatureAxis_tslaGigafactoryMember_20141017_20141017" decimals="-6" scale="6">195</ix:nonFraction> million of transferable tax credits, subject to capital investments by us and our partners for Gigafactory Nevada of at least $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000827" name="tsla:ExpectedCapitalInvestment" contextRef="C_0001318605_us-gaapGuaranteeObligationsByNatureAxis_tslaGigafactoryMember_20141017" decimals="-7" scale="9">3.50</ix:nonFraction>&#160;billion, which we exceeded during 2017, and specified hiring targets for Gigafactory Nevada, which we exceeded during 2018. We recorded these credits as earned when we had evidence there was a market for their sale. Credits were applied as a cost offset to either employee expense or to capital assets, depending on the source of the credits. Credits earned from employee hires or capital spending by our partners at Gigafactory Nevada were recorded as a reduction to operating expenses. As of December&#160;31, 2019 and 2018, we had earned the maximum of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000828" name="us-gaap:InvestmentTaxCredit" contextRef="C_0001318605_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_20190101_20191231" decimals="INF" scale="6"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000829" name="us-gaap:InvestmentTaxCredit" contextRef="C_0001318605_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_20180101_20181231" decimals="INF" scale="6">195</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction>&#160;million of transferable tax credits under these agreements. </p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000578" name="us-gaap:NewAccountingPronouncementsPolicyPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001318605_20190101_20191231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000578_dcnt_72c6ec5b-a05d-43ed-b225-38ab2d3b42da">
<p style="margin-top:13pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Recent Accounting Pronouncements</p>
<p style="margin-top:4pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Recently issued accounting pronouncements not yet adopted</p>
<p style="margin-top:4pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In June 2016, the FASB issued ASU No. 2016-13, Measurement of Credit Losses on Financial Instruments, to require financial assets carried at amortized cost to be presented at the net amount expected to be collected based on historical experience, current conditions and forecasts. Subsequently, the FASB issued ASU No. 2018-19, Codification Improvements to Topic 326, to clarify that receivables arising from operating leases are within the scope of lease accounting standards. Further, the FASB issued ASU No. 2019-04, ASU No. 2019-05, ASU 2019-10 and ASU 2019-11 to provide additional guidance on the credit losses standard. The ASUs are effective for interim and annual periods beginning after December 15, 2019, with early adoption permitted. Adoption of the ASUs is on a modified retrospective basis. We plan to adopt the ASUs on January 1, 2020. The ASUs are currently not expected to have a material impact on our consolidated financial statements.</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In January 2017, the FASB issued ASU No. 2017-04, Simplifying the Test for Goodwill Impairment, to simplify the test for goodwill impairment by removing Step 2. An entity will, therefore, perform the goodwill impairment test by comparing the fair value of a reporting unit with its carrying amount and recognizing an impairment charge for the amount by which the carrying amount exceeds the fair value, not to exceed the total amount of goodwill allocated to the reporting unit. An entity still has the option to perform a qualitative assessment to determine if the quantitative impairment test is necessary. The ASU is effective for interim and annual periods beginning after December 15, 2019, with early adoption permitted. Adoption of the ASU is prospective. We plan to adopt the ASU prospectively on January 1, 2020. The ASU is currently not expected to have a material impact on our consolidated financial statements.</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In August 2018, the FASB issued ASU No. 2018-15, Customer&#8217;s Accounting for Implementation Costs Incurred in a Cloud Computing Arrangement that Is a Service Contract. The ASU aligns the requirements for capitalizing implementation costs incurred in a hosting arrangement that is a service contract with the requirements for capitalizing implementation costs incurred to develop or obtain internal-use software (and hosting arrangements that include an internal-use software license). The ASU is effective for interim and annual periods beginning after December 15, 2019, with early adoption permitted. Adoption of the ASU is either retrospective or prospective. We plan to adopt the ASU prospectively on January 1, 2020. The ASU is currently not expected to have a material impact on our consolidated financial statements.</p></ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">88</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000527_dcnt_15c605dc-a634-47a0-a0ae-d82df516ede8"><ix:continuation id="F_000578_dcnt_72c6ec5b-a05d-43ed-b225-38ab2d3b42da">
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In December 2019, the FASB issued ASU No. 2019-12, Simplifying the Accounting for Income Taxes, as part of its initiative to reduce complexity in accounting standards. The amendments in the ASU are effective for fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2020, including interim periods therein. Early adoption of the standard is permitted, including adoption in interim or annual periods for which financial statements have not yet been issued. We have not early adopted this ASU for 2019.&#160;&#160;The ASU is currently not expected to have a material impact on our consolidated financial statements.</span></p>
<p style="margin-top:13pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Recently adopted accounting pronouncements</p>
<p style="margin-top:4pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;letter-spacing:-0.2pt;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In February 2016, the FASB issued ASU No.&#160;2016-02, Leases, to require lessees to recognize all leases, with limited exceptions, on the balance sheet, while recognition on the statement of operations will remain similar to legacy lease accounting, ASC 840. The ASU also eliminates real estate-specific provisions and modifies certain aspects of lessor accounting. Subsequently, the FASB issued ASU No.&#160;2018-10<span style="font-style:italic;">, Codification Improvements to Topic&#160;842</span>, ASU No.&#160;2018-11, <span style="font-style:italic;">Targeted Improvements</span>,<span style="font-style:italic;"> </span>ASU No.&#160;2018-20,<span style="font-style:italic;"> Narrow-Scope Improvements for Lessors</span>, and ASU 2019-01, <span style="font-style:italic;">Codification Improvements</span>, to clarify and amend the guidance in ASU No.&#160;2016-02. We adopted the ASUs on January&#160;1, 2019 on a modified retrospective basis through a cumulative adjustment to our beginning accumulated deficit balance. Prior comparative periods have not been recast under this method, and we adopted all available practical expedients, as applicable. Further, solar leases that commence on or after January&#160;1, 2019, where we are the lessor and which were accounted for as leases under ASC 840, will no longer meet the definition of a lease. Instead, solar leases commencing on or after January 1, 2019 will be accounted for under the new revenue standard. In addition to recognizing operating leases that were previously not recognized on the consolidated balance sheet, our build-to-suit leases were also de-recognized with a net decrease of approximately $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000830" name="us-gaap:CumulativeEffectOfNewAccountingPrincipleInPeriodOfAdoption" contextRef="C_0001318605_us-gaapAdjustmentsForNewAccountingPronouncementsAxis_us-gaapAccountingStandardsUpdate201602Member_us-gaapLeaseArrangementTypeAxis_tslaBuildToSuitLeaseArrangementMember_20190101" decimals="-6" sign="-" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="6">97</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million to our beginning accumulated deficit after income tax effects, as our build-to-suit leases no longer qualify for build-to-suit accounting and are instead recognized as operating leases. Upon adoption, our consolidated balance sheet include an overall reduction in assets of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000831" name="us-gaap:Assets" contextRef="C_0001318605_us-gaapAdjustmentsForNewAccountingPronouncementsAxis_us-gaapAccountingStandardsUpdate201602Member_20190101" decimals="-6" scale="6">473</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and a reduction in liabilities of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000832" name="us-gaap:Liabilities" contextRef="C_0001318605_us-gaapAdjustmentsForNewAccountingPronouncementsAxis_us-gaapAccountingStandardsUpdate201602Member_20190101" decimals="-6" scale="6">570</ix:nonFraction> million. The adoption of the ASUs did not have a material impact on the consolidated statement of operations or the consolidated statement of cash flows.</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In August 2017, the FASB issued ASU No.&#160;2017-12, <span style="font-style:italic;">Targeted Improvements to Accounting for Hedging Activities</span>, to simplify the application of current hedge accounting guidance. The ASU expands and refines hedge accounting for both non-financial and financial risk components and aligns the recognition and presentation of the effects of the hedging instrument and the hedged item in the financial statements. We adopted the ASU prospectively on January&#160;1, 2019, and the ASU did not have a material impact on the consolidated financial statements.</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In January 2018, the FASB issued ASU No.&#160;2018-01, <span style="font-style:italic;">Land Easement Practical Expedient Transition to Topic&#160;842</span>, to permit an entity to elect a practical expedient to not re-evaluate land easements that existed or expired before the entity&#8217;s adoption of ASU No.&#160;2016-02, <span style="font-style:italic;">Leases</span>, and that were not accounted for as leases. The ASU did not have a material impact on the consolidated financial statements.<span style="color:#000000;">&#160;</span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p></ix:continuation></ix:continuation><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000528" name="us-gaap:BusinessCombinationDisclosureTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001318605_20190101_20191231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000528_dcnt_346da676-b9e0-430b-bafc-30163b876a41">
<p style="margin-top:3pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Note 3 &#8211; Business Combinations</p>
<p style="margin-top:4pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Maxwell Acquisition</p>
<p style="margin-top:4pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000833" name="us-gaap:BusinessAcquisitionEffectiveDateOfAcquisition1" contextRef="C_0001318605_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_tslaMaxwellTechnologiesIncorporationMember_20190516_20190516" format="ixt:datemonthdayyearen">May 16, 2019</ix:nonNumeric> (the &#8220;Acquisition Date&#8221;), we completed our strategic acquisition of Maxwell Technologies, Inc. (&#8220;Maxwell&#8221;), an energy storage and power delivery products company, for its complementary technology and workforce. Pursuant to the related Agreement and Plan of Merger (the &#8220;Merger Agreement&#8221;), <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000834" name="tsla:BusinessCombinationCommonStockConversionBasis" contextRef="C_0001318605_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_tslaMaxwellTechnologiesIncorporationMember_20190101_20191231">each issued and outstanding share of Maxwell common stock was converted into <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000835" name="tsla:BusinessCombinationStockConversionRatio" contextRef="C_0001318605_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_tslaMaxwellTechnologiesIncorporationMember_20190516_20190516" decimals="INF" scale="-2">0.0193</ix:nonFraction> (the &#8220;Exchange Ratio&#8221;) shares of our common stock.</ix:nonNumeric> In addition, Maxwell&#8217;s stock option awards and restricted stock unit awards were assumed by us and converted into corresponding equity awards in respect of our common stock based on the Exchange Ratio, with the awards retaining the same vesting and other terms and conditions as in effect immediately prior to the acquisition. </p>
<p style="margin-top:13pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Fair Value of Purchase Consideration</p>
<p style="margin-top:4pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Acquisition Date fair value of the purchase consideration was $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000836" name="us-gaap:BusinessCombinationConsiderationTransferred1" contextRef="C_0001318605_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_tslaMaxwellTechnologiesIncorporationMember_20190516_20190516" decimals="-6" scale="6">207</ix:nonFraction> million (<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_000837" name="us-gaap:BusinessAcquisitionEquityInterestsIssuedOrIssuableNumberOfSharesIssued" contextRef="C_0001318605_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_tslaMaxwellTechnologiesIncorporationMember_20190516_20190516" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">902,968</ix:nonFraction> shares issued at $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD_xbrlishares" id="F_000838" name="us-gaap:BusinessAcquisitionSharePrice" contextRef="C_0001318605_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_tslaMaxwellTechnologiesIncorporationMember_20190516" decimals="INF">229.49</ix:nonFraction> per share, the opening price of our common stock on the Acquisition Date).</p></ix:nonNumeric>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">89</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000528_dcnt_346da676-b9e0-430b-bafc-30163b876a41" continuedAt="F_000528_dcnt_9acc4bc6-8f40-466b-99e5-04ba47e281a8">
<p style="margin-top:13pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Fair Value of Assets Acquired and Liabilities Assumed</span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:4.5pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We accounted for the acquisition using the purchase method of accounting for business combinations under ASC 805, <span style="font-style:italic;">Business Combinations</span>. The total purchase price is allocated to the tangible and identifiable intangible assets acquired and liabilities based on their estimated fair values as of the Acquisition Date.&#160;&#160; </p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Fair value estimates are based on a complex series of judgments about future events and uncertainties and rely heavily on estimates and assumptions. The judgments used to determine the estimated fair value assigned to each class of assets acquired and liabilities assumed, as well as asset lives and the expected future cash flows and related discount rates, can materially impact our consolidated financial statements. Significant inputs used for the model included the amount of cash flows, the expected period of the cash flows and the discount rates. In 2019, we finalized our estimate of the Acquisition Date fair values of the assets acquired and the liabilities assumed and there were no changes to the fair values of the assets acquired and the liabilities assumed.&#160;&#160;</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000587" name="us-gaap:ScheduleOfRecognizedIdentifiedAssetsAcquiredAndLiabilitiesAssumedTableTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001318605_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_tslaMaxwellTechnologiesIncorporationMember_20190101_20191231" escape="true">

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p></ix:continuation><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000530" name="us-gaap:FairValueDisclosuresTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001318605_20190101_20191231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000530_dcnt_3bdfa6c8-130f-4e5d-89ee-d8fff173c038">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:3pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Note 5 &#8211; Fair Value of Financial Instruments</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:4pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ASC&#160;820<span style="font-style:italic;">, Fair Value Measurements</span>, states that fair value is an exit price, representing the amount that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants. As such, fair value is a market-based measurement that should be determined based on assumptions that market participants would use in pricing an asset or a liability<span style="color:#000000;">. The three-tiered fair value hierarchy, which prioritizes which inputs should be used in measuring fair value, is comprised of: (Level&#160;I) observable inputs such as quoted prices in active markets&#59; (Level&#160;II) inputs other than quoted prices in active markets that are observable either directly or indirectly and (Level&#160;III) unobservable inputs for which there is little or no market data. The fair value hierarchy requires the use of observable market data when available in determining fair value. <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000591" name="us-gaap:ScheduleOfFairValueAssetsAndLiabilitiesMeasuredOnRecurringBasisTableTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001318605_20190101_20191231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000591_cnt_1">Our assets and liabilities that were measured at fair value on a recurring basis were as follows (in millions):</ix:nonNumeric></span></p><ix:continuation id="F_000591_cnt_1">

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">All of our money market funds were classified within Level&#160;I of the fair value hierarchy because they were valued using quoted prices in active markets. Our interest rate swaps were classified within Level&#160;II of the fair value hierarchy because they were valued using alternative pricing sources or models that utilized market observable inputs, including current and forward interest rates. During the year ended December&#160;31, 2019, there were no transfers between the levels of the fair value hierarchy.</p>
<p style="margin-top:13pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Interest Rate Swaps</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:4pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We enter into fixed-for-floating interest rate swap agreements to swap variable interest payments on certain debt for fixed interest payments, as required by certain of our lenders. We do not designate our interest rate swaps as hedging instruments. Accordingly, our interest rate swaps are recorded at fair value on the consolidated balance sheets within other assets or other long-term liabilities, with any changes in their fair values recognized as other income (expense), net, in the consolidated statements of operations and with any cash flows recognized as investing activities in the consolidated statements of cash flows. <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000592" name="us-gaap:ScheduleOfInterestRateDerivativesTableTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001318605_20190101_20191231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000592_cnt_1">Our interest rate swaps outstanding were as follows (in millions):</ix:nonNumeric></p>

As a result of the adoption of the new lease standard on January 1, 2019, we have de-recognized all build-to-suit lease assets and have reassessed these leases to be operating lease right-of-use assets within the consolidated balance sheet as of December&#160;31, 2019 (see Note 2, <span style="font-style:italic;">Summary of Significant Accounting Policies</span>).</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Construction in progress is primarily comprised of tooling and equipment related to the manufacturing of our products and Gigafactory Shanghai construction. Completed assets are transferred to their respective asset classes, and depreciation begins when an asset is ready for its intended use. Interest on outstanding debt is capitalized during periods of significant capital asset construction and amortized over the useful lives of the related assets. During the years ended December&#160;31, 2019 and 2018, we capitalized $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001061" name="us-gaap:InterestCostsCapitalized" contextRef="C_0001318605_20190101_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">31</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001062" name="us-gaap:InterestCostsCapitalized" contextRef="C_0001318605_20180101_20181231" decimals="-6" scale="6">55</ix:nonFraction> million, respectively, of interest.</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000533_dcnt_c35f62c4-5f55-486f-bb96-30bc170035d4">
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Panasonic has partnered with us on Gigafactory Nevada with investments in the production equipment that it uses to manufacture and supply us with battery cells. Under our arrangement with Panasonic, we plan to purchase the full output from their production equipment at negotiated prices. As the terms of the arrangement convey a finance lease under ASC 842, <span style="font-style:italic;">Leases</span>, we account for their production equipment as leased assets when production commences. This results in us recording the cost of their production equipment within property, plant and equipment, net, on the consolidated balance sheets with a corresponding liability recorded to debt and finance leases. As of December&#160;31, 2019<span style="color:#000000;"> and 2018, we had cumulatively capitalized costs of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001070" name="us-gaap:PropertyPlantAndEquipmentNet" contextRef="C_0001318605_us-gaapPropertyPlantAndEquipmentByTypeAxis_us-gaapEquipmentMember_20191231" decimals="-7" scale="9">1.73</ix:nonFraction>&#160;billion and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001071" name="us-gaap:PropertyPlantAndEquipmentNet" contextRef="C_0001318605_us-gaapPropertyPlantAndEquipmentByTypeAxis_us-gaapEquipmentMember_20181231" decimals="-7" scale="9">1.24</ix:nonFraction>&#160;billion, respectively,</span> on the consolidated balance sheets in relation to the production equipment under our Panasonic arrangement.<span style="color:#000000;"> We had cumulatively capitalized total costs for Gigafactory Nevada, including costs under our Panasonic arrangement, of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001072" name="us-gaap:ConstructionInProgressGross" contextRef="C_0001318605_us-gaapPropertyPlantAndEquipmentByTypeAxis_us-gaapManufacturingFacilityMember_20191231" decimals="-7" scale="9">5.27</ix:nonFraction>&#160;billion and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001073" name="us-gaap:ConstructionInProgressGross" contextRef="C_0001318605_us-gaapPropertyPlantAndEquipmentByTypeAxis_us-gaapManufacturingFacilityMember_20181231" decimals="-7" scale="9">4.62</ix:nonFraction>&#160;billion as of December&#160;31, 2019 and 2018, respectively.</span></p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In 2019, the Shanghai government agreed to provide $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001074" name="tsla:IncentivesManufacturingEquipmentInvestments" contextRef="C_0001318605_20190101_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">85</ix:nonFraction> million of certain incentives in connection with us making certain manufacturing equipment investments at Gigafactory Shanghai, of which $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001075" name="tsla:IncentivesReceivedInCash" contextRef="C_0001318605_20190101_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">46</ix:nonFraction> million was received in cash and the remaining $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001076" name="tsla:IncentivesReceivedInFormOfAssetsAndServices" contextRef="C_0001318605_20190101_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">39</ix:nonFraction> million was in the form of assets and services contributed by the government. As a result of the adoption of the new lease standard on January 1, 2019, we have de-recognized all build-to-suit lease liabilities and have reassessed these leases to be operating lease right-of-use liabilities as of December 31, 2019. </p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Due to price adjustments we made to our vehicle offerings during 2019, we increased our sales return reserve significantly on vehicles previously sold under our buyback options program. Refer to Note 2, <span style="font-style:italic;">Summary of Significant Accounting Policies</span>, for details on these transactions.</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:7pt;">&#160;</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000536" name="tsla:CustomerDepositsTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001318605_20190101_20191231" escape="true">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Note 11 &#8211; Customer Deposits</p>
<p style="margin-top:4pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Customer deposits primarily consisted of cash payments from customers at the time they place an order or reservation for a vehicle or an energy product and any additional payments up to the point of delivery or the completion of installation, including the fair values of any customer trade-in vehicles that are applicable toward a new vehicle purchase. <span style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;color:#212529;">Customer deposits also include prepayments on contracts that can be cancelled without significant penalties, such as vehicle maintenance plans.&#160;</span>Customer deposit amounts and timing vary depending on the vehicle model, the energy product and the country of delivery. In the case of a vehicle, customer deposits are fully refundable. In the case of an energy generation or storage product, customer deposits are fully refundable prior to the entry into a purchase agreement or in certain cases for a limited time thereafter (in accordance with applicable laws). Customer deposits are included in current liabilities until refunded or until they are applied towards the customer&#8217;s purchase balance. As of December&#160;31, 2019 and December&#160;31,&#160;2018, we held $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001112" name="tsla:CustomerDepositsLiabilitiesCurrent" contextRef="C_0001318605_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">726</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001113" name="tsla:CustomerDepositsLiabilitiesCurrent" contextRef="C_0001318605_20181231" decimals="-6" scale="6">793</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, respectively, in customer deposits. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">96</p>

<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Recourse debt refers to debt that is recourse to our general assets. Non-recourse debt refers to debt that is recourse to only assets of our subsidiaries. The differences between the unpaid principal balances and the net carrying values are due to convertible senior note conversion features, debt discounts or deferred financing costs. As of December&#160;31, 2019, we were in material compliance with all financial debt covenants, which include minimum liquidity and expense-coverage balances and ratios.</p>

<p style="margin-top:4pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Solar Bonds are senior unsecured obligations that are structurally subordinate to the indebtedness and other liabilities of our subsidiaries. Solar Bonds were issued under multiple series with various terms and interest rates. Additionally, we have assumed the <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001448" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentInterestRateStatedPercentage" contextRef="C_0001318605_us-gaapDebtInstrumentAxis_tslaFivePointFiveZeroPercentSeniorConvertibleNoteDueTwentyTwentyTwoMember_us-gaapLongtermDebtTypeAxis_us-gaapSeniorNotesMember_20191231" decimals="INF" scale="-2">5.50</ix:nonFraction>% Convertible Senior Notes due in 2022 issued by Maxwell, which are convertible into shares of our common stock as a result of our acquisition of Maxwell. </p>
<p style="margin-top:13pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Automotive Asset-backed Notes</p>
<p style="margin-top:4pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">From time to time, we transfer receivables or beneficial interests related to certain leased vehicles into SPEs and issue Automotive Asset-backed Notes, backed by these automotive assets to investors. The SPEs are consolidated in the financial statements. The cash flows generated by these automotive assets are used to service the principal and interest payments on the Automotive Asset-backed Notes and satisfy the SPEs&#8217; expenses, and any remaining cash is distributed to the owners of the SPEs. We recognize revenue earned from the associated customer lease contracts in accordance with our revenue recognition policy. The SPEs&#8217; assets and cash flows are not available to our other creditors, and the creditors of the SPEs, including the Automotive Asset-backed Note holders, have no recourse to our other assets. A third-party contracted with us to provide administrative and collection services for these automotive assets. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In November 2019, we issued $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001449" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentFaceAmount" contextRef="C_0001318605_us-gaapDebtInstrumentAxis_tslaAutomotiveAssetBackedNotesMember_20191130" decimals="-6" scale="6">861</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million in aggregate principal amount of Automotive Asset-backed Notes. <p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:13pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Solar Asset-backed Notes</span></p>
<p style="margin-top:4pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">From time to time, our subsidiaries pool and transfer either qualifying solar energy systems and the associated customer contracts or our interests in certain financing funds into Special Purpose Entities (&#8220;SPEs&#8221;) and issue Solar Asset-backed Notes backed by these solar assets or interests to investors. The SPEs are wholly owned by us and are consolidated in the financial statements. The cash flows generated by these solar assets or distributed by the underlying financing funds to certain SPEs are used to service the principal and interest payments on the Solar Asset-backed Notes and satisfy the SPEs&#8217; expenses, and any remaining cash is distributed to us. We recognize revenue earned from the associated customer contracts in accordance with our revenue recognition policy. The SPEs&#8217; assets and cash flows are not available to our other creditors, and the creditors of the SPEs, including the Solar Asset-backed Note holders, have no recourse to our other assets. We contracted with the SPEs to provide operations &#38; maintenance and administrative services for the solar energy systems. As of December&#160;31, 2019, solar assets pledged as collateral for Solar Asset-backed Notes had a carrying value of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001451" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentCollateralAmount" contextRef="C_0001318605_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_tslaSolarCityMember_us-gaapDebtInstrumentAxis_tslaSolarAssetBackedNotesMember_us-gaapLongtermDebtTypeAxis_tslaNonrecourseDebtMember_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">690</ix:nonFraction> million and are included within solar energy systems, net, on the consolidated balance sheets.</p>
<p style="margin-top:13pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;<span style="font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">China Loan Agreements</span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:4pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In March 2019, one of our subsidiaries entered into a loan agreement with a syndicate of lenders in China for a bridge loan to be used for expenditures related to the construction of and production at our Gigafactory Shanghai. The loan agreement was terminated in December 2019. <span style="color:#000000;">&#160;</span>&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In September 2019, one of our subsidiaries entered into a loan agreement with a lender in China for an unsecured 12-month revolving facility of up to RMB <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217CNY" id="F_001452" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityMaximumBorrowingCapacity" contextRef="C_0001318605_us-gaapDebtInstrumentAxis_tslaChinaLoanAgreementsMember_us-gaapLongtermDebtTypeAxis_tslaUnsecuredRevolvingFacilityMember_20190930" decimals="INF" scale="9">5.0</ix:nonFraction> billion (or the equivalent drawn in U.S. dollars), to <span style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;">finance vehicles in-transit to China</span>. Borrowed funds bear interest at an annual rate no greater than <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001453" name="tsla:DebtInstrumentAnnualInterestRateAsPercentageOfOneYearLoanInterestRateQuotedByBank" contextRef="C_0001318605_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_us-gaapDebtInstrumentAxis_tslaChinaLoanAgreementsMember_us-gaapLongtermDebtTypeAxis_tslaUnsecuredRevolvingFacilityMember_us-gaapVariableRateAxis_tslaPeoplesBankOfChinaOneYearRateMember_20190901_20190930" decimals="INF" scale="-2">90</ix:nonFraction>% of the one-year rate published by the People&#8217;s Bank of China. The loan facility is non-recourse to our assets.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In <p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:13pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Cash Equity Debt </p>
<p style="margin-top:4pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In connection with the cash equity financing deals closed in 2016, our subsidiaries issued $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001462" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentFaceAmount" contextRef="C_0001318605_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_tslaSolarCityMember_us-gaapDebtInstrumentAxis_tslaCashEquityDebtMember_us-gaapLongtermDebtTypeAxis_tslaNonrecourseDebtMember_20161231" decimals="-6" scale="6">502</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million in aggregate principal amount of debt that bears interest at fixed rates. This debt is secured by, among other things, our interests in certain financing funds and is non-recourse to our other assets.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:13pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Solar Loan-backed Notes</p>
<p style="margin-top:4pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In January 2016 and January 2017, our subsidiaries pooled and transferred certain MyPower customer notes receivable into two SPEs and issued $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001463" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentFaceAmount" contextRef="C_0001318605_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_tslaSolarCityMember_us-gaapDebtInstrumentAxis_tslaSolarLoanBackedNotesMember_us-gaapLongtermDebtTypeAxis_tslaNonrecourseDebtMember_us-gaapVariableRateAxis_tslaInterestRateClassAMember_20160131" decimals="-6" scale="6"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001464" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentFaceAmount" contextRef="C_0001318605_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_tslaSolarCityMember_us-gaapDebtInstrumentAxis_tslaSolarLoanBackedNotesMember_us-gaapLongtermDebtTypeAxis_tslaNonrecourseDebtMember_us-gaapVariableRateAxis_tslaInterestRateClassAMember_20170131" decimals="-6" scale="6">330</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction>&#160;million in aggregate principal amount of Solar Loan-backed Notes, backed by these notes receivable to investors. <span style="color:#000000;">Accordingly, we did not recognize a gain or loss on the transfer of these notes receivable. </span>The SPEs are wholly owned by us and are consolidated in the financial statements. The payments received by the SPEs from these notes receivable are used to service the semi-annual principal and interest payments on the Solar Loan-backed Notes and satisfy the SPEs&#8217; expenses, and any remaining cash is distributed to us. The SPEs&#8217; assets and cash flows are not available to our other creditors, and the creditors of the SPEs, including the Solar Loan-backed Note holders, have no recourse to our other assets.</p></ix:continuation>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">103</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000537_dcnt_f84d226c-6fd7-4ff5-88eb-0c87e596e4c2" continuedAt="F_000537_dcnt_3a6c06f2-cac0-485d-bda8-c4851d70eaff">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:13pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Warehouse Agreements</span></p>
<p style="margin-top:4pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In August 2016, our subsidiaries entered into a loan and security agreement (the &#8220;2016 Warehouse Agreement&#8221;) for borrowings secured by the future cash flows arising from certain leases and the associated leased vehicles. On August&#160;17, 2017, the 2016 Warehouse Agreement was amended to modify the interest rates and extend the availability period and the maturity date, and our subsidiaries entered into another loan and security agreement (the &#8220;2017 Warehouse Agreement&#8221;) with substantially the same terms as and that shares the same committed amount with the 2016 Warehouse Agreement. On August&#160;16, 2018, the 2016 Warehouse Agreement and 2017 Warehouse Agreement were amended to extend the availability period from August&#160;17, 2018 to August&#160;16, 2019 and extend the maturity date from September 2019 to <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:F_001465">September 2020</span>. On December 28, 2018, our subsidiaries terminated the 2017 Warehouse Agreement after having fully repaid all obligations thereunder, and entered into a third loan and security agreement with substantially the same terms as and that shares the same committed amount with the 2016 Warehouse Agreement. We refer to these agreements together as the &#8220;Warehouse Agreements.&#8221; Amounts drawn under the Warehouse Agreements generally bear interest at a fixed margin above (i) LIBOR or (ii) the commercial paper rate. The Warehouse Agreements are non-recourse to our other assets.</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Pursuant to the Warehouse Agreements, an undivided beneficial interest in the future cash flows arising from certain leases and the related leased vehicles has been sold for legal purposes but continues to be reported in the consolidated financial statements. The interest in the future cash flows arising from these leases and the related vehicles is not available to pay the claims of our creditors other than pursuant to obligations to the lenders under the Warehouse Agreements.<span style="color:#000000;"> </span>Any excess cash flows not required to pay obligations under the Warehouse Agreements are available for distributions.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In August 2019, our subsidiaries amended the Warehouse Agreements to extend the availability period from August 16, 2019 to August 14, 2020 and extend the maturity date from September 2020 to <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:F_001466">September 2021</span>.</p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In November 2019, we repaid $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001467" name="us-gaap:RepaymentsOfSecuredDebt" contextRef="C_0001318605_us-gaapDebtInstrumentAxis_tslaWarehouseAgreementMember_us-gaapLongtermDebtTypeAxis_tslaNonrecourseDebtMember_20191101_20191130" decimals="-6" scale="6">723</ix:nonFraction> million of the principal outstanding under the Warehouse Agreements.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:13pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Solar Term Loans</p>
<p style="margin-top:4pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our subsidiaries have entered into agreements for term loans with various financial institutions. <span style="color:#000000;">The term loans are secured by substantially all of the assets of the subsidiaries, including its interests in certain financing funds, and are non-recourse to our other assets.</span></p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During the fourth quarter of 2019, we fully repaid the $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001468" name="us-gaap:RepaymentsOfLongTermDebt" contextRef="C_0001318605_us-gaapDebtInstrumentAxis_tslaSolarCityTermLoansMember_us-gaapLongtermDebtTypeAxis_tslaNonrecourseDebtMember_20191001_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">159</ix:nonFraction> million in aggregate principal of one term loan. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:13pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Canada Credit Facility</p>
<p style="margin-top:4pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In December 2016, one of our subsidiaries entered into a credit agreement (the &#8220;Canada Credit Facility&#8221;) with a bank for borrowings secured by our interests in certain vehicle leases. In December 2017 and December 2018, the Canada Credit Facility was amended to add our interests in additional vehicle leases as collateral, allowing us to draw additional funds. Amounts drawn under the Canada Credit Facility bear interest at fixed rates. The Canada Credit Facility is non-recourse to our other assets.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:13pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Solar Renewable Energy Credit and other Loans</p>
<p style="margin-top:4pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We have entered into various solar renewable energy credit and other loan agreements with various financial institutions, including a solar revolving credit facility. The solar renewable energy credit loan facility is secured by substantially all of the assets of <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_tslaSubsidiary" id="F_001469" name="tsla:NumberOfWhollyOwnedSubsidiariesReceivedRemainingCashDistributions" contextRef="C_0001318605_us-gaapDebtInstrumentAxis_tslaSolarRenewableEnergyCreditAndOtherLoansMember_20191231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">one</ix:nonFraction> of our wholly owned subsidiaries, including its rights under forward contracts to sell SRECs, and is non-recourse to our other assets. The solar revolving credit facility is secured by certain assets of the subsidiary and is non-recourse to our other assets.</p></ix:continuation>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p></ix:continuation><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000538" name="tsla:LesseeOperatingAndFinanceLeasesDisclosureTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001318605_20190101_20191231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000538_dcnt_150f0596-a23e-4b4d-87f5-b80edeaabdab">
<p style="margin-top:3pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Note 13 &#8211; Leases</p>
<p style="margin-top:4pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We have entered into various non-cancellable operating and finance lease agreements for certain of our offices, manufacturing and warehouse facilities, retail and service locations, equipment, vehicles, and solar energy systems, worldwide. We determine if an arrangement is a lease, or contains a lease, at inception and record the leases in our financial statements upon lease commencement, which is the date when the underlying asset is made available for use by the lessor. </p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our leases, where we are the lessee, often include options to extend the lease term for up to <span><ix:nonNumeric id="F_001509" name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseTermOfContract" contextRef="C_0001318605_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_20191231" format="ixt-sec:duryear"><ix:nonNumeric id="F_001510" name="us-gaap:LesseeFinanceLeaseTermOfContract1" contextRef="C_0001318605_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_20191231" format="ixt-sec:duryear">10</ix:nonNumeric></ix:nonNumeric> years</span>. Some of our leases also include options to terminate the lease prior to the end of the agreed upon lease term. For purposes of calculating lease liabilities, lease terms include options to extend or terminate the lease when it is reasonably certain that we will exercise such options. </p>
<p style="margin-top:9pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Lease expense for operating lease payments is recognized on a straight-line basis over the lease term. Certain operating leases provide for annual increases to lease payments based on an index or rate. We calculate the present value of future lease payments based on the index or rate at the lease commencement date for new leases commencing after January 1, 2019. For historical leases, we used the index or rate as of the adoption date. Differences between the calculated lease payment and actual payment are expensed as incurred. Lease expense for finance lease payments is recognized as amortization expense of the finance lease ROU asset and interest expense on the finance lease liability over the lease term. </p></ix:nonNumeric>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">105</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000539" name="us-gaap:ShareholdersEquityAndShareBasedPaymentsTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001318605_20190101_20191231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000539_dcnt_d66e1534-e824-4204-afa1-85a4b975be14">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:3pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Note 14 &#8211; Equity Incentive Plans</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:4pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In June 2019, we adopted the 2019 Equity Incentive Plan (the &#8220;2019 Plan&#8221;), and simultaneously terminated the 2010 Equity Incentive Plan (the &#8220;2010 Plan&#8221;). <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_001596" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardOptionsGrantsInPeriodGross" contextRef="C_0001318605_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_tslaTwoThousandAndTenEquityIncentivePlanMember_20190101_20191231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">No</ix:nonFraction> new awards have been granted under the 2010 Plan following the adoption of the 2019 Plan, but such termination did not affect outstanding awards under the 2010 Plan. The 2019 Plan has similar terms as the 2010 Plan and provides for the granting of stock options, restricted stock, RSUs, stock appreciation rights, performance units and performance shares to our employees, directors and consultants. Stock options granted under the 2019 Plan may be either incentive stock options or nonstatutory stock options. Incentive stock options may only be granted to our employees. Nonstatutory stock options may be granted to our employees, directors and consultants. Generally, our stock options and RSUs vest over <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001594" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardAwardVestingPeriod1" contextRef="C_0001318605_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapRestrictedStockUnitsRSUMember_20190101_20191231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen"><ix:nonNumeric id="F_001593" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardAwardVestingPeriod1" contextRef="C_0001318605_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapEmployeeStockOptionMember_20190101_20191231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">four years</ix:nonNumeric></ix:nonNumeric> and our stock options are exercisable over a maximum period of <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001595" name="us-gaap:DeferredCompensationArrangementWithIndividualMaximumContractualTerm1" contextRef="C_0001318605_20190101_20191231" format="ixt-sec:duryear">10</ix:nonNumeric> years from their grant dates. Vesting typically terminates when the employment or consulting relationship ends.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As of December&#160;31, 2019, <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_001597" name="us-gaap:CommonStockCapitalSharesReservedForFutureIssuance" contextRef="C_0001318605_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_tslaTwoThousandAndNineteenEquityIncentivePlanMember_20191231" decimals="INF" scale="6">11</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million shares were reserved and available for issuance under the 2019 Plan.</p></ix:nonNumeric>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000539_dcnt_3e7cab9b-746f-410f-bcbd-ce4d689d38e2" continuedAt="F_000539_dcnt_8e3bdc8f-ae46-41e3-944f-681449cfeb21">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The fair value of RSUs with service or service and performance conditions is measured on the grant date based on the closing fair market value of our common stock. The risk-free interest rate is based on the U.S. Treasury yield for zero-coupon U.S. Treasury notes with maturities approximating each grant&#8217;s expected life. Prior to the fourth quarter of 2017, given our then limited history with employee grants, we used the &#8220;simplified&#8221; method in estimating the expected term of our employee grants&#59; the simplified method utilizes the average of the time-to-vesting and the contractual life of the employee grant. Beginning with the fourth quarter of 2017, we use our historical data in estimating the expected term of our employee grants. The expected volatility is based on the average of the implied volatility of publicly traded options for our common stock and the historical volatility of our common stock.</span></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Stock-based compensation expense associated with each tranche under the 2018 CEO Performance Award is recognized over the longer of (i) the expected achievement period for the operational milestone for such tranche and (ii) the expected achievement period for the related market capitalization milestone determined on the grant date, beginning at the point in time when the relevant operational milestone is considered probable of being met. If such operational milestone becomes probable any time after the grant date, we will recognize a cumulative catch-up expense from the grant date to that point in time. If the related market capitalization milestone is achieved earlier than its expected achievement period and the achievement of the related operational milestone, then the stock-based compensation expense will be recognized over the expected achievement period for the operational milestone, which may accelerate the rate at which such expense is recognized. </p></ix:continuation>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On December&#160;22, 2017, the 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (&#8220;Tax Act&#8221;) was enacted into law making significant changes to the Internal Revenue Code. Changes include, but are not limited to, a federal corporate tax rate decrease from <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001788" name="us-gaap:EffectiveIncomeTaxRateReconciliationAtFederalStatutoryIncomeTaxRate" contextRef="C_0001318605_20170101_20171231" decimals="INF" scale="-2">35</ix:nonFraction>% to <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001789" name="us-gaap:EffectiveIncomeTaxRateReconciliationAtFederalStatutoryIncomeTaxRate" contextRef="C_0001318605_20190101_20191231" decimals="INF" scale="-2"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001790" name="us-gaap:EffectiveIncomeTaxRateReconciliationAtFederalStatutoryIncomeTaxRate" contextRef="C_0001318605_20180101_20181231" decimals="INF" scale="-2">21</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction>% for tax years beginning after December&#160;31, 2017, the transition of U.S. international taxation from a worldwide tax system to a territorial system and a one-time transition tax on the mandatory deemed repatriation of foreign earnings. We were required to recognize the effect of the tax law changes in the period of enactment, such as re-measuring our U.S. deferred tax assets and liabilities as well as reassessing the net realizability of our deferred tax assets and liabilities. The Tax Act did not give rise to any material impact on the consolidated balance sheets and consolidated statements of operations due to our historical worldwide loss position and the full valuation allowance on our net U.S. deferred tax assets.</p>

The valuation allowance on our net deferred taxes increased by $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001824" name="us-gaap:ValuationAllowanceDeferredTaxAssetChangeInAmount" contextRef="C_0001318605_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_tslaSolarCityMember_20190101_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">150</ix:nonFraction> million, decreased by $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001825" name="us-gaap:ValuationAllowanceDeferredTaxAssetChangeInAmount" contextRef="C_0001318605_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_tslaSolarCityMember_20180101_20181231" decimals="-6" sign="-" scale="6">38</ix:nonFraction> million, and increased by $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001826" name="us-gaap:ValuationAllowanceDeferredTaxAssetChangeInAmount" contextRef="C_0001318605_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_tslaSolarCityMember_20170101_20171231" decimals="-6" scale="6">821</ix:nonFraction> million during the years ended December&#160;31, 2019, 2018 and 2017, respectively. The changes in valuation allowance are primarily due to additional U.S. deferred tax assets and liabilities incurred in the respective year. We have net $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001827" name="us-gaap:DeferredTaxAssetsNet" contextRef="C_0001318605_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityAxis_tslaForeignJurisdictionsMember_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">151</ix:nonFraction> million of deferred tax assets in foreign jurisdictions, which management believes are more-likely-than-not to be fully realized given the expectation of future earnings in these jurisdictions. We continue to monitor the realizability of the U.S. deferred tax assets taking into account multiple factors, including the results of operations and magnitude of excess tax deductions for stock-based compensation. We intend to continue maintaining a full valuation allowance on our U.S. deferred tax assets until there is sufficient evidence to support the reversal of all or some portion of these allowances. Release of all, or a portion, of the valuation allowance would result in the recognition of certain deferred tax assets and a decrease to income tax expense for the period the release is recorded.</p>

A portion of these losses were generated by SolarCity prior to our acquisition in 2016 and, therefore, are subject to change of control provisions, which limit the amount of acquired tax attributes that can be utilized in a given tax year. We do not expect these change of control limitations to significantly impact our ability to utilize these attributes.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As of December&#160;31, 2019, we had research and development tax credits of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001865" name="us-gaap:DeferredTaxAssetsTaxCreditCarryforwardsResearch" contextRef="C_0001318605_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityAxis_us-gaapDomesticCountryMember_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">320</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001866" name="us-gaap:DeferredTaxAssetsTaxCreditCarryforwardsResearch" contextRef="C_0001318605_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityAxis_us-gaapStateAndLocalJurisdictionMember_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">284</ix:nonFraction> million for federal and state income tax purposes, respectively. If not utilized, the federal research and development tax credits will expire in various amounts beginning in <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001867" name="tsla:ResearchTaxCreditCarryForwardExpirationDates" contextRef="C_0001318605_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityAxis_us-gaapDomesticCountryMember_20190101_20191231">2024</ix:nonNumeric>. However, the state research and development tax credits can be carried forward indefinitely. In addition, we have other general business tax credits of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001868" name="us-gaap:DeferredTaxAssetsTaxCreditCarryforwardsGeneralBusiness" contextRef="C_0001318605_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityAxis_us-gaapDomesticCountryMember_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">125</ix:nonFraction> million for federal income tax purposes, which will not begin to significantly expire until <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001869" name="tsla:TaxCreditCarryForwardExpirationYear" contextRef="C_0001318605_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityAxis_us-gaapDomesticCountryMember_20190101_20191231">2033</ix:nonNumeric>.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001870" name="us-gaap:DeferredTaxLiabilitiesUndistributedForeignEarnings" contextRef="C_0001318605_20191231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">No</ix:nonFraction> deferred tax liabilities for foreign withholding taxes have been recorded relating to the earnings of our foreign subsidiaries since all such earnings are intended to be indefinitely reinvested. The amount of the unrecognized deferred tax liability associated with these earnings is immaterial.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Federal and state laws can impose substantial restrictions on the utilization of net operating loss and tax credit carry-forwards in the event of an &#8220;ownership change,&#8221; as defined in Section&#160;382 of the Internal Revenue Code. We have determined that no significant limitation would be placed on the utilization of our net operating loss and tax credit carry-forwards due to prior ownership changes.</p></ix:continuation>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As of December&#160;31, 2019, accrued interest and penalties related to unrecognized tax benefits are classified as income tax expense and were immaterial. Unrecognized tax benefits of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001882" name="tsla:UnrecognizedTaxBenefitsOfDeferredTaxAccountingThatWouldNotImpactAnnualEffectiveRate" contextRef="C_0001318605_20191231" decimals="-6" scale="6">247</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, if recognized, would not affect our effective tax rate since the tax benefits would increase a deferred tax asset that is currently fully offset by a full valuation allowance. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We file income tax returns in the U.S., California and various state and foreign jurisdictions. We are currently under examination by the IRS for the years <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001883" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxExaminationYearUnderExamination" contextRef="C_0001318605_srtRangeAxis_srtMinimumMember_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityNameAxis_us-gaapInternalRevenueServiceIRSMember_20190101_20191231">2015</ix:nonNumeric> and <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001884" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxExaminationYearUnderExamination" contextRef="C_0001318605_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityNameAxis_us-gaapInternalRevenueServiceIRSMember_20190101_20191231">2016</ix:nonNumeric>. Additional tax years within the period <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001885" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxExaminationYearUnderExamination" contextRef="C_0001318605_srtRangeAxis_srtMinimumMember_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityAxis_us-gaapDomesticCountryMember_20190101_20191231">2004</ix:nonNumeric> to <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001886" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxExaminationYearUnderExamination" contextRef="C_0001318605_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityAxis_us-gaapDomesticCountryMember_20190101_20191231">2018</ix:nonNumeric> remain subject to examination for federal income tax purposes, and tax years <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001887" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxExaminationYearUnderExamination" contextRef="C_0001318605_srtRangeAxis_srtMinimumMember_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityAxis_stprCA_20190101_20191231">2004</ix:nonNumeric> to <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001888" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxExaminationYearUnderExamination" contextRef="C_0001318605_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityAxis_stprCA_20190101_20191231">2018</ix:nonNumeric> remain subject to examination for California income tax purposes. All net operating losses and tax credits generated to date are subject to adjustment for U.S. federal and California income tax purposes. Tax years <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001889" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxExaminationYearUnderExamination" contextRef="C_0001318605_srtRangeAxis_srtMinimumMember_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityAxis_tslaUnitedStatesAndForeignJurisdictionsMember_20190101_20191231">2008</ix:nonNumeric> to <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001890" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxExaminationYearUnderExamination" contextRef="C_0001318605_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityAxis_tslaUnitedStatesAndForeignJurisdictionsMember_20190101_20191231">2018</ix:nonNumeric> remain subject to examination in other U.S. state and foreign jurisdictions.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The potential outcome of the current examination could result in a change to unrecognized tax benefits within the next twelve months. However, we cannot reasonably estimate possible adjustments at this time.&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:9pt;text-indent:5.24%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The U.S. Tax Court issued a decision in <span style="font-style:italic;">Altera Corp v. Commissioner</span> related to the treatment of stock-based compensation expense in a cost-sharing arrangement. On June 7, 2019, the Court reversed the Tax Court decision and upheld the validity of Treas. Reg. Section 1.482-7A(d)(2), requiring stock-based compensation costs be included in the costs shared under a cost sharing agreement. Given that the current active decision can still be appealed because Altera has the option to petition up to the Supreme Court, Tesla&#8217;s position is to continue to include stock-based compensation in cost sharing allocation agreement. If and when the current tax court&#8217;s decision is overturned, we will treat the amount previously shared as a pre-payment to future cost sharing agreement costs. Because we have a full valuation allowance in the U.S., any potential tax benefits would increase our U.S. deferred tax asset and would not have a material impact to our financials.</p>
